Title: Toward the Observability of Cloud-Native Applications: The Overview of the State-of-the-Art
Authors: J. Kosińska, B. Baliś, M. Konieczny, M. Malawski, S. Zieliński
Gaps_and_Limitations: Lack of unified terminology; absence of formal reference architectures; early stage of AIOps automation; high toolchain integration complexity.
Roadmap_Pillars: Development of maturity models; deeper eBPF integration for low-overhead visibility; FinOps and GreenOps alignment.
Abstract: Cloud-native applications (CNAs) deployed in dynamic containerized environments require observability beyond traditional monitoring. This study provides a comprehensive overview of the state-of-the-art in CNA observability, analyzing approaches, requirement types, and architectural tooling across infrastructure and microservices.

Title: A Survey on Observability of Distributed Edge & Container-Based Microservices
Authors: M. Usman, S. Ferlin, A. Brunstrom, J. Taheri
Gaps_and_Limitations: Absence of formal reference architectures; severe operational complexity due to stack fragmentation; telemetry scalability and cross-domain correlation challenges.
Roadmap_Pillars: Intelligent automation via AI/ML (AIOps); security integration (SecOps); enhancing developer experience (DevEx); unified observability platforms.
Abstract: Distributed edge and container-based microservices introduce severe challenges for performance debugging and fault localization. This survey reviews telemetry collection methods, open-source frameworks, and correlation strategies across distributed microservice topologies.

Title: Observability in Microservices: An In-Depth Exploration of Frameworks, Challenges, and Deployment Paradigms
Authors: U. Faseeha, H. Jamil Syed, F. Samad, S. Zehra, H. Ahmed
Tools_Analyzed: Cilium, Hubble, Istio, Envoy, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus
Gaps_and_Limitations: Conceptual confusion between monitoring and observability; lack of practical multi-pillar architectures; difficulties tracing failures in ephemeral container deployments.
Roadmap_Pillars: Evolution of frameworks for modern deployment paradigms (service mesh, event-driven); automated telemetry analytics; optimization of observability runtime overhead.
Abstract: Investigates microservice observability across emerging deployment paradigms, comparing sidecar proxies and eBPF-based kernel instrumentation for real-time performance tracking in Kubernetes.

Title: A Systematic Mapping Study on Observability of Microservices-Based Applications: Fundamentals, Classifications, and Challenges
Authors: F. Gomes, P. Rego, F. Trinta
Tools_Analyzed: Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Kubernetes HPA, KEDA, Grafana
Gaps_and_Limitations: Difficulty in correlating multimodal telemetry data; inadequacy of traditional monitoring for sophisticated CNAs; complex root cause analysis for autoscaling.
Roadmap_Pillars: Advanced ML-based resource management; automated diagnostic mechanisms coupled with autoscaling controllers; low-overhead real-time collection.
Abstract: A systematic mapping study analyzing 66 studies on microservices observability, establishing classifications, benchmark datasets, and challenges in triggering automated autoscaling in cloud-native platforms.

Title: Holistic Root Cause Analysis for Failures in Cloud-Native Systems Through Observability Data
Authors: Y. Han, Q. Du, Y. Huang, P. Li, X. Shi, J. Wu, P. Fang, F. Tian, C. He
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Services Computing (Vol. 17, No. 6)
Gaps_and_Limitations: Inconsistent problem definitions for Root Cause Analysis (RCA); high cloud-native heterogeneity across traces, metrics, and logs; high correlation computation costs.
Roadmap_Pillars: Scalable multimodal data correlation algorithms; graph attention networks for dynamic service topologies; automated mitigation workflows.
Abstract: Addresses inconsistent problem formulations in cloud-native failure diagnosis by proposing a holistic root cause localization model based on multimodal observability data and topology graph learning.

Title: Cloud-Native Computing: A Survey From the Perspective of Services
Authors: S. Deng, H. Zhao, B. Huang, C. Zhang, F. Chen, Y. Deng, J. Yin, S. Dustdar, A. Y. Zomaya
Venue: Proceedings of the IEEE (Vol. 112, No. 1, pp. 12-46)
Gaps_and_Limitations: Missing unified research roadmaps for cloud-native lifecycles; heavy cognitive load for developers (DevEx); lack of integrated runtime security telemetry.
Roadmap_Pillars: Integration of SecOps with performance telemetry; improvement of Developer Experience (DevEx); observability optimization for serverless and green computing.
Abstract: Surveys cloud-native computing across service design, orchestration, and lifecycle operations, detailing architectural patterns, observability requirements, and green computing research directions.

Title: Observability in Fog Computing
Authors: A. Araujo, B. Costa, J. Bachiega Jr, L. R. Carvalho, R. Buyya
Gaps_and_Limitations: Scarcity of holistic reference architectures; severe resource constraints (CPU/memory overhead) in distributed fog/edge nodes; device heterogeneity.
Roadmap_Pillars: Lightweight AI/ML for local anomaly detection (TinyML); standardized interoperability protocols; adaptive low-overhead observability frameworks.
Abstract: Formalizes observability lifecycle phases across heterogeneous fog computing nodes, discussing edge resource constraints and adaptive multi-tier telemetry collection.

Title: Anomaly Detection in Cloud-Native B5G Systems Using Observability and Machine Learning COTS Solutions
Authors: G. Z. Bruno, R. L. Santos, M. C. Luizelli, L. R. Bays
Venue: Journal of Internet Services and Applications (Vol. 14, No. 1)
Gaps_and_Limitations: Heavy bias toward metrics over logs/traces in B5G research; excessive memory and CPU overhead of CNOT stacks; unstandardized log structures.
Roadmap_Pillars: Distributed tracing integration; scalability analysis of COTS ML detectors; non-intrusive observability in Open RAN disaggregated components.
Abstract: Evaluates anomaly detection in cloud-native Beyond-5G testbeds using commercial-off-the-shelf observability stacks, benchmarking resource overhead and metric-centric detection accuracy.

Title: Observability for Cloud Native Platforms
Venue: Master's Thesis (Häme University of Applied Sciences)
Tools_Analyzed: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo, OpenTelemetry Collector
Gaps_and_Limitations: High integration complexity in multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters; configuration divergence between OTel and native collectors; high storage ingestion costs.
Roadmap_Pillars: Benchmark evaluations of LGTM (Loki, Grafana, Tempo, Mimir) vs OTel collector architectures; automated retention and sampling pipelines.
Abstract: Designs and benchmarks an open-source cloud-native observability platform on Kubernetes, evaluating end-to-end telemetry pipelines, correlation mechanisms, and operational costs.

Title: A Map of Cloud-Native Practices and Tools to Achieve Desirable System Qualities
Authors: H. Wei, N. Madhavji, J. Steinbacher
Venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Software Architecture (ICSA 2025)
Gaps_and_Limitations: Lack of a systematic bridge connecting desirable software qualities with concrete cloud-native tools; limited empirical validation across production settings.
Roadmap_Pillars: Continuous evolution interfaces for quality-to-tool mappings; comprehensive industrial validation beyond initial expert consensus.
Abstract: Maps cloud-native architectural practices and open-source tooling against system qualities based on literature review and industrial expert evaluations.
